title: Pervasive interactions between exposures and polygenic risk can inform more effective clinical and behavioral interventions.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hits. Nature article page redirects to a login. Read the data and code availability statements of the open medRxiv/PMC preprint (PMC11312673).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: n = 408,801 UK Biobank participants, 7 diseases, 75 contexts (exposures such as diet, social factors, metabolites), 24,198 PGS×C models (models testing whether a polygenic score's effect changes with context), 746 significant. Preprint says individual-level data require a UK Biobank application; the supplementary tables (S1–S5) hold only summary statistics per exposure and disease.

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level genotypes and phenotypes are UK Biobank controlled access and need an approved application (stated in the preprint's data availability). This is controlled access, not open. The only open outputs are summary tables and a promised R Shiny app.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files. The disease outcomes exist only in UK Biobank. The open supplement holds per-model interaction statistics, which would have to be repurposed as labels.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked. Genotypes and exposures are UK Biobank only.

a5_enough_rows.note: 408,801 participants per the paper, but none are accessible. The open summary tables cover only significant exposure–disease pairs (count not seen).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The open summary outputs (interaction strength, proportion needed to benefit) are themselves statistical-model outputs computed from UK Biobank, so they are not physical measurements.

honest_claim_h3: Not reached: data are controlled access.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a person's inherited genetic risk score plus lifestyle and social exposures to predict who develops seven common diseases.
plain_idea.train_on: UK Biobank participants (408,801 per the paper; not verified), each with a polygenic score (a genetic risk score summed over many DNA variants) and 75 exposure measurements.
plain_idea.predict: Diagnosis of each of seven diseases, taken from UK Biobank hospital and health records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would show which exposures amplify genetic risk, so interventions could target the people who benefit most; but only with an approved UK Biobank application.

ml_idea: Gene–environment interaction modelling of disease risk; it needs UK Biobank individual-level access, so it is not feasible as an open-data project.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Data availability statement: UK Biobank application required. Already failed.

verdict_reason: A1 fails. All individual-level data are UK Biobank controlled access (needs an application). The only open outputs are summary statistics from the authors' own models, with no full text or supplement open from the journal.
